body:
## Problem

Hundreds of files carry stale copyright years. For example, many files in `python/kserve/kserve/models/` still read `# Copyright 2019 The KServe Authors.` even though it is now 2026. The breakdown:

| Year | Count (python/kserve) |
|------|----------------------|
| 2019 | 56 |
| 2020 | 45 |
| 2021 | 85 |
| 2022 | 44 |
| 2023 | 88 |
| 2024 | 15 |
| 2025 | 12 |
| 2026 | 1  |

## Root cause

Two mechanisms conspire to keep years stale:

1. **`hack/boilerplate.sh`** only inserts a copyright header when a file has _none_. It never updates an existing year.
2. **`make generate`** (Makefile `generate` target) explicitly caches copyright years before running `openapi-generator` and restores them afterward, preventing the generator from ever advancing the year.

## Expected behavior

Copyright years should reflect the year of the last material change to each file, or at minimum a CI check should flag files whose copyright year is more than one calendar year stale so contributors can update them as part of normal development.

## Proposed fix

- Update `hack/boilerplate.sh` to detect files whose copyright year is older than the current year and update them (or optionally just the files modified in the current year via `git log`).
- Consider adding a `make check-copyright` target that fails CI when a file last modified in year Y still carries year Y-N (for configurable N).
- Remove the copyright-year-preservation logic from `make generate` so that re-generating a model file advances its year.

## Scope

Affects at minimum:
- `python/kserve/kserve/models/` (generated OpenAPI models)
- `python/kserve/test/` (generated test stubs)
- Potentially Go files in `pkg/` and `cmd/`
title: bug: stale copyright years across Python SDK and generated files

body:
### Summary

When deploying an InferenceService with `autoscalerClass: "keda"` and a Prometheus metric trigger (following the [[official KServe KEDA autoscaler guide](https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/predictive-inference/autoscaling/keda-autoscaler/)](https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/predictive-inference/autoscaling/keda-autoscaler/)), KServe creates a ScaledObject that fails to generate a valid HPA.

The resulting error message is:

```
failed to ensure HPA is correctly created for ScaledObject: HorizontalPodAutoscaler.autoscaling "keda-hpa-qwen3-single-node-predictor" is invalid: spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization: Invalid value: 0: must be greater than 0
```

---

### Environment

* **KServe version:** v0.15.0 (Helm install)
* **KEDA version:** v2.15.0 (Helm install)
* **Kubernetes version:** v1.30
* **Deployment mode:** Standard (not RawDeployment)
* **Prometheus setup:** kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart
* **Runtime:** vLLM (custom ClusterServingRuntime)

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy the following InferenceService:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
   kind: InferenceService
   metadata:
     name: qwen3-single-node
     namespace: sunny
     annotations:
       serving.kserve.io/deploymentMode: "Standard"
       serving.kserve.io/autoscalerClass: "keda"
   spec:
     predictor:
       minReplicas: 1
       maxReplicas: 5
       model:
         modelFormat:
           name: huggingface
         runtime: vllm-single-node-rocm
         storageUri: pvc://models-nfs-pvc/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
       autoScaling:
         metrics:
           - type: External
             external:
               metric:
                 backend: "prometheus"
                 serverAddress: "http://kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090"
                 query: vllm:num_requests_running
               target:
                 type: Value
                 value: "2"
   ```

2. Observe the ScaledObject and HPA creation.

---

### Observed Behavior

* A ScaledObject is created, but the corresponding HPA creation fails with:

  ```
  spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization: Invalid value: 0: must be greater than 0
  ```
* Adding a CPU resource metric resolves that particular error, but then the ScaledObject generates an invalid CPU utilization value (`824671889656`), causing another failure:

  ```
  error parsing cpu metadata: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "824671889656": value out of range
  ```
* When I manually edit that value in the deployed ScaledObject YAML, the HPA is created and autoscaling works.

---

### Expected Behavior

KServe should:

* Generate a valid ScaledObject and HPA when only a Prometheus metric is used for scaling.
* Omit any CPU metric or default `averageUtilization` value if not explicitly defined.

---

### Additional Info

* The Prometheus metric (`vllm:num_requests_running`) resolves correctly and returns non-zero values.
* The ServiceMonitor configuration is correct, and Prometheus shows the metric as expected.
* The KEDA team has confirmed this integration is managed on the KServe/Knative side.
* This issue may originate from the logic in KServe that generates the ScaledObject spec when using the KEDA autoscaler class.
title: KServe KEDA autoscaler creates invalid HPA (averageUtilization: 0) and invalid CPU metric value when using Prometheus trigger

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]
When the src uri is `s3://REDACTED/model` and an object exists in `REDACTED/model/checkpoints/model.ckpt`,
it is downloaded to `tmp/models/model/model.ckpt` instead of `tmp/models/model/checkpoints/model.ckpt` instead.

```bash
docker run --env-file env.lists3 -it storage-init:test s3://REDACTED/model /tmp/models                                                             
INFO [initializer-entrypoint:<module>():16] Initializing, args: src_uri [s3://REDACTED/model] dest_path[ [/tmp/models]
INFO [storage.py:download():64] Copying contents of s3://REDACTED/model to local
INFO [storage.py:_download_s3():276] Downloaded object model/checkpoints/model.ckpt to /tmp/models/model.ckpt
INFO [storage.py:_download_s3():276] Downloaded object model/sec.yaml to /tmp/models/sec.yaml
INFO [storage.py:download():110] Successfully copied s3://REDACTED/model to /tmp/models
INFO [storage.py:download():111] Model downloaded in 1.116252792 seconds.
```

Was downloaded to
```
├── model.ckpt
└── sec.yaml
```
instead of 
```
├── checkpoints
│     ├── model.ckpt
└── sec.yaml

```

Seems like this is introduced from this fixed issue https://github.com/kserve/kserve/issues/3200 from this [line](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/storage/storage.py#L257-L260)

Was fixed by renaming the base path in my s3 bucket, so the src_uri provided is changed from `s3://REDACTED/model` to `s3://REDACTED/models` so it didn't coincide with the file `model.ckpt`

**What did you expect to happen:**
Files should be downloaded to the correct folder
```
...
INFO [storage.py:_download_s3():276] Downloaded object models/checkpoints/model.ckpt to /tmp/models/checkpoints/model.ckpt
...
```

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

If you enable logging, the agent sidecar added breaks streaming responses.   Instead of a streamed responses, the caller only gets any response data after the full response has been created.


**What did you expect to happen:**

The streamed response should start and the caller should see each streamed token as they are generated.

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**

Here is the fully functional LLM inference service using a public docker image that can be used to reproduce the problem.
Normally, we have a custom logger to handle the logging, but I have omitted it to simply this example.

custom-model.yaml:
```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-model
spec:
  predictor:
   # Adding the logger, introduces the agent sidecar which breaks streaming responses
   # Comment out to get expected behavior.
   logger:
      mode: all
   containers:
    - name: kserve-container
      image: jjharrow/facebook-pt-125m-service
      env:
        - name: BENTOML_HOME
          value: /home/bentoml/bento
      args:
        - openllm
        - start
        - --port
        - "8080"
        - --backend=pt
        - --dtype=float32
        - facebook/opt-125m
      ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
```

kubectl apply -f  custom-model.yaml

Once successfully deployed/started get the service address

`HOST={inferenceServiceAddress}`

You can show the behavior using the script `read-stream.sh` to invoke a streaming inference and show timestamps on the responses.   When streaming properly the first response takes about 3-4 secs for me, with the rest completing over the next 5 seconds or so (depending on how long the response is).   When logging is enabled, instead the first response takes 8 seconds with all the output essentially happening at the same time.

read-stream.sh
```
#/bin/bash
# Usage: read-stream.sh http://custom-model.default.cluster.local
HOST=$1

printf '[%s]\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
curl -s $HOST/v1/generate_stream -H 'accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "What is the meaning of life?"}' \
  | while IFS= read -r line; do printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$line"; done
```

With logging enabled:

```
./read-stream.sh $HOST
[2024-07-19 10:52:49]
[2024-07-19 10:52:57] data: {"prompt":"What is the meaning of life?","finished":false,"outputs":[{"index":0,"text":"\n","token_ids":[50118],"cumulative_logprob":0.0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":null}],"prompt_token_ids":[2,2264,16,5,3099,9,301,116],"prompt_logprobs":null,"request_id":"openllm-200254079ce84ebda5980c34bffd0d24"}
...
[2024-07-19 10:52:58] data: [DONE]
```

With logging disabled:
```
./read-stream.sh $HOST
[2024-07-19 10:55:59]
[2024-07-19 10:56:03] data: {"prompt":"What is the meaning of life?","finished":false,"outputs":[{"index":0,"text":"\n","token_ids":[50118],"cumulative_logprob":0.0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":null}],"prompt_token_ids":[2,2264,16,5,3099,9,301,116],"prompt_logprobs":null,"request_id":"openllm-7977401451b14bb59c13e92865a91047"}
...
[2024-07-19 10:56:07] data: [DONE]
```

From a python environment you can demonstrate it with the openllm.   It is more visual since you can see each word print one at a time, instead of getting the whole response in a single print.

```
pip install openllm==0.4.44 openllm-client==0.4.44
openllm query --endpoint $HOST hello
hello! i'm a new player too! i just started playing. i just want to know what i can do to improve my game. i have a lot of stuff to learn but i'm not sure if i can really improve my game in a very specific way. i'm also new to this game and i'm learning alot. i just want to know if i can improve my game or if i should just continue playing and play. thanks!

Hello, i'm a new player too! i just started playing. i just want to know what i can do to improve my game. i have a lot of stuff to learn but
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**

I have an InferenceService `my-classifier`.

When i try to `curl` from another pod inside the same namespace, it works fine when the domain name is all lowercase (expectedly), but it doesn't when there are some uppercase letters (404 not found). 

But if i try to `curl` the private service created by knative (`my-classifier-predictor-00001-private`), it works for both cases (i'm guessing bcos it doesn't go through Istio).

{
  "status": "alive"
}
```

**What did you expect to happen:**
I expect `curl http://MY-Classifier.test.svc.cluster.local` to work, since DNS names aren't case sensitive. 

My use case is that the application code i'm writing which will be talking to kserve models may have uppercase letters in the domain name. I can always make it all lowercase in the application code too, but I feel like we should solve this on the kserve/knative/istio side.

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: my-classifier
  namespace: test
spec:
  ...
status:

  url: http://my-classifier.test.svc.cluster.local

**Anything else you would like to add:**
This is the `VirtualService` created by KServe for this `InferenceService`:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: my-classifier
  namespace: test
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: InferenceService
    name: my-classifier
  ...
spec:

  - knative-serving/knative-local-gateway

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
I have a local cluster without internet access. Manifests version 1.8 is deployed on it. I deployed this version using images imported as tar files. I also imported the image for InferenceService as a tar file. However, the service does not start. If you run the command `microk8s kubectl describe inferenceservices -n kubeflow-namespace llm`, you may see the following error message:
```
Revision "llm -predictor-00001" failed with message: Unable to fetch image "yurkoff/torchserve-kfs:0.9.0-gpu": failed to resolve image to digest: Get "https://index.docker.io/v2 /": read tcp 10.1.22.219:48238->54.198.86.24:443: read: connection reset by peer.
```

Moreover, the image is present in microk8s ctr...
`microk8s ctr images list | grep yurkoff`
```
docker.io/yurkoff/torchserve-kfs:0.9.0-gpu                                                                                                     application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json      sha256:1b771d7c0c2d26f78e892997cb00e6051c77cf3654827c4715aa5a502267ee76 5.7 GiB    linux/amd64                                                                                             io.cri-containerd.image=managed
```

In machine with internet:
```
microk8s ctr images pull docker.io/yurkoff/torchserve-kfs:0.9.0-gpu

```
In local machine without internet:
```
microk8s ctr images import yurkoff_torchserve-kfs_0.9.0-gpu.tar
microk8s kubectl apply -f llm_isvc.yaml
```


**What did you expect to happen:**
Successful deployment of InferenceService

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: "llm"

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Created a InferenceGraph with custom annotation: `custom.annotation/hostname: xxx` this annotaton is not propagated to downstream Knative service.

**What did you expect to happen:**
Expect this annotation to be propagated to downstream KNative Service

**What's the InferenceGraph yaml:**
```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: InferenceGraph
metadata:
  annotations:
    custom.annotation/hostname: test
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: test
  name: test
  namespace: default
spec:
  nodes:
    root:
      routerType: Sequence
      steps:
        - name: test-transformer
          serviceName: test-transformer
        - data: $response
          name: test-predictor
          serviceName: test-predictor
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**
There is a precedence for passthrough annotation `serving.knative.openshift.io/enablePassthrough: 'true'` That is explicitly passed [here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/56b8fe0d189fc0d557e9a8af07eab0c12852d5fd/pkg/controller/v1alpha1/inferencegraph/knative_reconciler.go#L163)

This ability to pass annotations is convenient because it allows to dynamically generate dns records using tools such as external-dns on istio `virtualService`

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

When defining an InferenceService with the modelmesh annotation it's suppose to be able to handle transformers by delegating the reconciling of it to the kserve controller instead of the modelmesh serving one. One issue I'm hitting is that it is currently only working if the underlying deployment mode is `Serverless` and not `RawDeployment`. This appears to be only a problem of the logic "falling through" an if statement here: https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/controller/v1beta1/inferenceservice/components/transformer.go#L171


Since the inferenceService is using ModeMesh as it's deployment mode, it's not covered in the check for creating the service for the transformer. That seems to be a mistake and not intentional as there's no hard dependency to using serverless for modelmesh.

Instead the controller should fall back on the `defaultDeploymentMode` entry in the configmap to figure out which deployment mode should be used to create the transformer deployment and services.


**What did you expect to happen:**

Transformers should not try and create a knative service when using a ModelMesh predictor and KServe is deployed using RawDeployment mode. 


**What's the InferenceService yaml:**

```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/deploymentMode: ModelMesh
  name: resnet
  namespace: kserve
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: onnx
      name: ""
      storage:
        key: localMinIO
        path: resnet
  transformer:
    containers:
    - args:
      - --model_name
      - resnet
      - --predictor_protocol
      - grpc-v2
      command:
      - python
      - -m
      - custom_transformer.model_grpc
      image: custom-image-transformer-grpc:v0.1.5
      name: kserve-container
      ports:
      - containerPort: 8081
        name: h2c
        protocol: TCP
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 2Gi
        requests:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 2Gi
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**
I've got a working fix locally that I will create a PR for and attach to this issue shortly.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]
With decoder-only models, such as GPT-2 padding should be done on the left. This is because the output is a continuation of the input prompt -- there would be gaps in the output without left padding. Huggingface will warn if we don't use left padding for decoder models. 
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/18388#issuecomment-1204369688
The huggingface will throw a warning about this
```
A decoder-only architecture is being used, but right-padding was detected! For correct generation results, please set padding_side='left' when initializing the tokenizer
```

**What did you expect to happen:**
It should pad left for decoder only models.


**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
[To help us debug please run `kubectl get isvc $name -n $namespace -oyaml` and paste the output]
```yaml

metadata:
  name: huggingface-gpt2
spec:

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

We have added a [fallback pad token if it is not already present in the tokenizer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/11e0ab2ca4d852ec154156fad4f9d220c8768d78/python/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/model.py#L130-L131) as part of the PR #3459. /kind bug

KServe's [ISVC CRD](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/config/crd/serving.kserve.io_inferenceservices.yaml) is too large and it's impossible to add new fields to the spec given the limitation of K8s CRD size in general.

This currently blocks a couple of community PRs, including https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/3479 and https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/3418.

Even though the error message is pointing to the annotations, the actual problem might be the size of the entire CRD. 
`CustomResourceDefinition "[inferenceservices.serving.kserve.io](http://inferenceservices.serving.kserve.io/)" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long: must have at most 262144 bytes`

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Given a cluster with a high count of Secrets (in the order of about 8k secrets), when and ISVC is reconciled the KServe controller tries to load into memory all Secrets in the cluster. Because the high count of Secrets, the KServe controller will reach its memory limit and the cluster will kill the pod. The cluster may re-create the pod but, given unchanged conditions, the pod will be killed continuously.

**What did you expect to happen:**
KServe controller should work fine even if the cluster has a high count of Secrets.

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
Not relevant. Any ISVC will lead to the crash.

**Anything else you would like to add:**
On a quick code review, looks like KServe catches the secrets when using an informer/watch. However, KServe may not need to watch for changes in Secrets and, apparently, Secrets are always queried by name. If this is true, it may be better to query directly the API Server rather than via a cache of the Secrets, preventing the need of an Informer/watch.

**Environment:**
- KServe Version: 0.11.2 - should also happen in  `master`
title: Controller out-of-memory kill when cluster has too many secrets

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
- Modify `test_bert_sequence_classification()` in `huggingfaceserver/test_model.py` such that the two input instances have different length:
```
% git diff huggingfaceserver/test_model.py
--- a/python/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/test_model.py
+++ b/python/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/test_model.py
@@ -62,7 +62,8 @@ def test_bert_sequence_classification():
     model.load()
 
     request = "Hello, my dog is cute."
-    response = asyncio.run(model({"instances": [request, request]}, headers={}))
+    request_2 = "Hello, my dog is cute. I love him."
+    response = asyncio.run(model({"instances": [request, request_2]}, headers={}))
     assert response == {"predictions": [1, 1]}
```
- Run the modified test: `pytest -v -W ignore -k "test_bert_sequence_classification"`
- This will fail with:
```
ValueError: Unable to create tensor, you should probably activate truncation and/or padding with 'padding=True' 'truncation=True'
to have batched tensors with the same length. Perhaps your features (`input_ids` in this case) 
have excessive nesting (inputs type `list` where type `int` is expected).
```
Full logs: [test.txt](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/files/14293621/test.txt)

- In short, the problem is that because the inputs have different lengths, they can’t be converted to fixed-size tensors

**What did you expect to happen:**
I expect that we are able to supply inputs of different length in a single batch.

**Potential fix:**
Based on the error, it seems like we need to add paddings, which is documented [here](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/pad_truncation) by hugging face.

> Batched inputs are often different lengths, so they can’t be converted to fixed-size tensors. Padding and truncation are strategies for dealing with this problem, to create rectangular tensors from batches of varying lengths. Padding adds a special padding token to ensure shorter sequences will have the same length as either the longest sequence in a batch or the maximum length accepted by the model. Truncation works in the other direction by truncating long sequences.
>
> In most cases, padding your batch to the length of the longest sequence and truncating to the maximum length a model can accept works pretty well. However, the API supports more strategies if you need them. The three arguments you need to are: padding, truncation and max_length.

So we should add `padding=True` (or `"longest"`, same behaviour, but more explicit) when calling `self.tokenizer()`, which will pad the inputs to the longest sequence in the batch, so that all inputs will have the same length.

I'm willing to contribute a fix for this. I've tested it locally and it works, but I'll add more rigorous tests as well, perhaps also see if we need truncation as well or just padding.

**Environment:**

- KServe Version: commit [e21b913](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/commit/e21b913fe10b377d72e67fbf92955dbcedd6f465)

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]
In transformer postprocess I am setting the parameters which also contains a float value. But in the end response, the float value is truncated to int. The transformer uses REST v2(OIP) protocol.
```python
def postprocess(self, response: InferResponse, headers: Dict[str, str]=None) -> dict:
        return_parameters = {"threshold":  0.4, "revision": "/mnt/models"}
        print(f"Returning: {return_parameters}")
        response.outputs[0]._parameters = return_parameters
        return response
```
I did some logging in the transformer and I get the float as expected: 
`Returning: {'threshold': 0.6, 'revision': '/mnt/models'}`. 

but the response received:
```python
{
    "model_name": "treatment1",
    "model_version": None,
    "id": "",
    "parameters": None,
    "outputs": [
        {
            "name": "OUTPUT__0",
            "shape": [1],
            "datatype": "FP32",
            "parameters": {"threshold": 0, "revision": "/mnt/models"},
            "data": [0.12074008584022522],
        }
    ],
}
```

**What did you expect to happen:**
Float values should not be truncated in parameters

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
[To help us debug please run `kubectl get isvc $name -n $namespace -oyaml` and paste the output]

**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]
This is because of the way parameters type hints defined. https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/e21b913fe10b377d72e67fbf92955dbcedd6f465/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v2_datamodels.py#L25. Since `int` is defined first, the pydantic tries to converts it to int. So the value is truncated.
We can resolve this by using [strict types](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/types/#pydantic.types.StrictInt) instead. 
Related #2754.
For more info read, https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions, https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/strict_mode/

body:
/kind bug

First of all, I'd like to say thank you for the work on KServe! It's been delightful so far playing around with KServe. But we found a small bug while testing out the HuggingFace model server (which we're aware is a very new addition as well).

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
1. Created an InferenceService using the HuggingFace model server (yaml pasted below)
2. Specified an s3 bucket as the `model_dir` (I suspect this might happen for anything that's not a local dir)
3. Observed that the model is succesfully downloaded to a tmp directory and loaded, but then encountered the `FileNotFoundError` right after

Logs:
```
% k logs huggingface-predictor-00003-deployment-8659bb8b9-m945b
Defaulted container "kserve-container" out of: kserve-container, queue-proxy
INFO:root:Copying contents of s3://kserve-test-models/classifier to local

INFO:kserve:successfully loaded tokenizer for task: 4

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/runpy.py", line 196, in _run_module_as_main
    return _run_code(code, main_globals, None,
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/runpy.py", line 86, in _run_code
    exec(code, run_globals)
  File "/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/__main__.py", line 69, in <module>
    kserve.ModelServer(registered_models=HuggingfaceModelRepository(args.model_dir)).start(
  File "/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/huggingface_model_repository.py", line 24, in __init__
    self.load_models()
  File "/kserve/kserve/model_repository.py", line 37, in load_models
    for name in os.listdir(self.models_dir):
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 's3://kserve-test-models/spam-classifier'
```


**What did you expect to happen:**

I expected that this would work, as the model was successfully downloaded and loaded. But I did find a tmp workaround below and I think I know where the issue is!

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: huggingface
spec:
  predictor:
    serviceAccountName: huggingface-sa
    containers:
    - args:
      - --model_name=spam-classifier
      # - --model_id=xyz (see workaround below)
      - --model_dir=s3://kserve-test-models/classifier
      - --tensor_input_names=input_ids
      image: kserve/huggingfaceserver:latest
      name: kserve-container
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**

A temporary workaround I found is to supply the `model_id` argument. It can have any value, as the `model_dir` will override it anyway during loading:

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/5172dc80b0a23d2263757de70a02eeef08b18811/python/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/model.py#L91-L94

<details>
  <summary>I have verified that this workaround works (expand to see logs).</summary>

```
% k logs huggingface-predictor-00004-deployment-946b4d6c8-pk5nj -f
Defaulted container "kserve-container" out of: kserve-container, queue-proxy
INFO:root:Copying contents of s3://kserve-test-models/classifier to local
INFO:root:Downloaded object classifier/config.json to /tmp/tmppwjsica7/config.json
...
INFO:kserve:successfully loaded tokenizer for task: 4
INFO:kserve:successfully loaded huggingface model from path /tmp/tmppwjsica7
INFO:kserve:Registering model: classifier
INFO:kserve:Setting max asyncio worker threads as 5
INFO:kserve:Starting uvicorn with 1 workers
2024-02-09 18:57:33.228 uvicorn.error INFO:     Started server process [1]
2024-02-09 18:57:33.229 uvicorn.error INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
2024-02-09 18:57:33.234 1 kserve INFO [start():62] Starting gRPC server on [::]:8081
2024-02-09 18:57:33.234 uvicorn.error INFO:     Application startup complete.
2024-02-09 18:57:33.235 uvicorn.error INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8080 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```
</details>

I think the issue is here:
https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/5172dc80b0a23d2263757de70a02eeef08b18811/python/huggingfaceserver/huggingfaceserver/__main__.py#L63-L72

1. `model.load()` will succeed, so we jump to line 68
2. It checks for `args.model_id`, which is empty, so we go inside the if block
3. It will try to instantiate `HuggingfaceModelRepository` with `model_dir`, which is pointing to an s3 bucket and not a local directory, thus causing the `FileNotFoundError`
4. This is how I came up with the workaround of passing `model_id`, so that the else block is executed instead (because the model did load succesfully, so doing `kserve.ModelServer().start([model] if model.ready else [])` won't be a problem)

Hi! In attempting to pass `InferInput.parameters` from a transformer to a predictor I realised the request reaching the predictor had completely removed the parameters.

This can be replicated with:

```python
import numpy as np
from kserve import InferRequest, InferInput

test_array = np.zeros((2, 2, 1), dtype="uint8")

test_input = InferInput(name="test", shape=test_array.shape, datatype="UINT8", parameters={"hello": "world"})
test_input.set_data_from_numpy(test_array)

test_infer = InferRequest(model_name="test", infer_inputs=[test_input])

print(test_infer.inputs[0].parameters)

test_infer.to_rest()
```

Output:
```terminal
{'hello': 'world', 'binary_data_size': 4}

{'id': None,
 'inputs': [{'name': 'test',
   'shape': (2, 2, 1),
   'datatype': 'UINT8',
   'data': None}]}
```

And is expected from looking at the code as the parameters are not handled:

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/c52753519e1802e73581856b1ae3a0f2f178d457/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/infer_type.py#L271-L329

Which is called by the `_X_predict` functions in the `kserve.Model` class.

**What did you expect to happen:**
I expect the parameters to be preserved when using the `to_rest/grpc` methods.

Am I mis-understanding something about parameters in that this is expected behaviour?

N/A

- Kserve has [conversion webhook](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/config/default/inferenceservice_conversion_webhook.yaml) in the inferenceservice CRD but modelmesh does not have it. 
- CRD will stay even though kserve controller is uninstalled. 
- inferenceservice CRD still looks for kserve controller as a webhook server even after kserve operator is uninstalled. That's why modelmesh controller failed to run.

~~~
  conversion:
    strategy: Webhook
    webhook:
        conversionReviewVersions: ["v1beta1"]
        clientConfig:
          # this is "\n" used as a placeholder, otherwise it will be rejected by the apiserver for being blank,
          # but we're going to set it later using the cert-manager (or potentially a patch if not using cert-manager)
          caBundle: Cg==
          service:
            namespace: $(kserveNamespace)
            name: $(webhookServiceName)
            path: /convert
~~~

At the moment, I removed the conversion webhook from CRD to solve this issue. However, if kserve api version is changed, the conversion webhook should be added then this issue will be back. 

What would be a good idea to solve this issue?

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

Support for collocating transformer and predictor in a single pod for custom models is introduced by the PR #2873. 
However, This allows the user to specify storage uri in both the transformer and predictor containers. This may introduce some problems.

For example, the user can specify two different storage uris in predictor and transformer, storage container does not support adding two storage uris. so what happens is the storage container takes the uri from the first container (the order containers specified in yaml). 

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-transformer-collocation
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - name: kserve-container
        image: kserve/custom-model-grpc:latest
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --grpc_port=8082
          - --http_port=8080
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-1    # different uri, this model will be downloaded
        
      - image: kserve/image-transformer:latest
        name: transformer-container   
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --protocol=grpc-v2
          - --http_port=8000
          - --grpc_port=8081
          - --predictor_host=localhost:8082
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8000
            protocol: TCP
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-2       # different uri, this is ignored by the storage initalizer
```

Another know problem is if the first container does not specy the strorage uri, then the storage initializer is not injected even if the second container has the storage uri.
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-transformer-collocation
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - name: kserve-container
        image: kserve/custom-model-grpc:latest
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --grpc_port=8082
          - --http_port=8080
                                                                                # no storage uri, storage initializer won't be injected.
        
      - image: kserve/image-transformer:latest
        name: transformer-container    
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --protocol=grpc-v2
          - --http_port=8000
          - --grpc_port=8081
          - --predictor_host=localhost:8082
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8000
            protocol: TCP
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-2       # ignored by the storage initalizer
```

**Solution:**
Restrict the storage uri env variable to predictor only and use the same model for transformer.
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-transformer-collocation
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - name: kserve-container
        image: kserve/custom-model-grpc:latest
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --grpc_port=8082
          - --http_port=8080
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-1    # download this model and use it for both predictor and transformer
        
      - image: kserve/image-transformer:latest
        name: transformer-container    
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --protocol=grpc-v2
          - --http_port=8000
          - --grpc_port=8081
          - --predictor_host=localhost:8082
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8000
            protocol: TCP
```

Add a validation to check if storage uri env variable is present in the transformer container. if it is present then, deny the resource creation.

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-transformer-collocation
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - name: kserve-container
        image: kserve/custom-model-grpc:latest
        args:
          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --grpc_port=8082
          - --http_port=8080
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-1 
        
      - image: kserve/image-transformer:latest

          - --model_name=custom-model
          - --protocol=grpc-v2
          - --http_port=8000
          - --grpc_port=8081

        ports:

            protocol: TCP
        env:
           - key: STORAGE_URI
             value: gs://some-uri-2       # the resource creation will be denied.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

When we specify two different priority for the same modelFormat with different versions,  the runtime selection becomes unpredictable. 

For example, Here is two serving runtimes. The MLServer runtime specifies two different priority for the 'sklearn' model with different version. At the same time Kserve sklearn runtime also has support for the 'sklearn' model with priority of 1.

Note: The runtimes are truncated for brevity.

**MLServer runtime**
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-mlserver
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
    - name: sklearn
      version: "0"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 1
    - name: sklearn
      version: "1"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 2
```
**Kserve sklearn runtime**
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-sklearnserver
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
    - name: sklearn
      version: "1"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 1
```
When we apply the following yaml , The MLServer runtime should be selected as it has the higher priority which is 2. But instead Kserve Sklearn runtime is selected.

**InferenceService**
```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "sklearn-iris"
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: sklearn
      protocolVersion: "v2"
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model" 
```
This is due to the fact that MLServer has two different priorities and one of which is lower i.e. 1. We didn't specify the model version in the isvc, so three of the model formats are valid for this isvc. 

When the runtime is sorted by the supported model's priority at first MLserver  precedes  the Sklearn because of the modelformat with priority value of 2. At the second round Sklearn gets the precedence because of mlserver's modelformat with priority value of 1.

**What did you expect to happen:**
The MLServer runtime should be selected. 


**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]
We should add a validation for this edge case.

Secondly, the "AWS_CA_BUNDLE" (serving.kserve.io/s3-cabundle) should specify the path to the certificate file, not the certificate content itself, but there seems to be no way to attach the CA bundle certificate file to the container.

I intend to address the first issue with a new pr. As for the second issue, I believe [this PR](The purpose of this issue is to consolidate unresolved issues that were previously created for similar problems and work towards resolving them together) will resolve it, but the problem is that this PR has been stagnant for approximately 5 months.

Considering the critical nature of our customers relying on self-signed certificates, I believe it is imperative to accelerate the resolution of this matter.

**What did you expect to happen:**
1. `serving.kserve.io/s3-verifyssl: '0'`  => Skip verification of SSL
2.  `serving.kserve.io/s3-cabundle: $PATH` option should work with a way to attach a secret to the container.

body:
/kind question

**What's the question**
I found that a pod created by KServe takes long time to be terminated (300 seconds).
As I understand, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` in the pod config controls this behavior and we can configure it per InferenceService by `timeout` (Ref: https://github.com/kserve/kserve/issues/1546). 
However, I'd like to decrease this value for all ISVC in our platform, because they take too long time to evict their pods during K8S node operation.
Would it be possible to set a default value of InferenceService's timeout? 

Btw, the below shows my experiment with adjusting a default value at KNative Serving side. It doesn't work.

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: pytorch-mnist
  namespace: default
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: pytorch
      storageUri: gs://kfserving-examples/models/torchserve/image_classifier/v2

```

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
1. Set a default value of `revision-timeout-seconds` in KNative 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/component: controller
    app.kubernetes.io/name: knative-serving
  name: config-defaults
  namespace: knative-serving
data:
  revision-timeout-seconds: "120"
```
2. Restart KNative controller
3. Deploy the above KServe's InferenceService
4. `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` in InferenceService's pod is still set to `300`


**Environment:**

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Updating the kserve manifests in kubeflow/manifests from v0.10 -> v0.11 (PR kubeflow/manifests#2504) causes the CI to fail when executing the `kserve tests` job.
The complete execution can be found  [here](https://github.com/kubeflow/manifests/actions/runs/5831759378/job/15815819933).

This error is blocking the Kubeflow 1.8 release as we cannot sync the latest manifests.

**What did you expect to happen:**
The CI of that repository executes the tests correctly and all tests succeed.

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
N/A

**Anything else you would like to add:**
The root cause could be the recent changes done in `kserve_kubeflow.yaml`, where a lot of annotations and field values are have replaced `kubeflow` with `kserve`. For example:

[Here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/install/v0.11.0/kserve_kubeflow.yaml#L20761)
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from: kserve/serving-cert
  creationTimestamp: null
```
while in the previous version of kserve, the [manifests](https://github.com/kubeflow/manifests/blob/master/contrib/kserve/kserve/kserve_kubeflow.yaml#L20234C1-L20238C58) in kubeflow/manifests had a different value:
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from: kubeflow/serving-cert
```

These are just examples, but there are several different fields that changed from `kubeflow` to `kserve`.

**Potential fix**
@annajung found out that reverting back the `kubeflow` values actually helps solving the CI error.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

Kserve uses Docker/Moby BuildKit for creating container images. However, the way how builds are performed depends on the Buildkit driver that is used. When using a "docker" driver (which seems to be the default on Linux), the container image is also loaded from the build cache to the persistent Docker storage for image, so that a subsequent "docker push" will succeed. However, when using the driver "docker-container" (as this seems to be the default on macOS), the image is _not_ automatically loaded to Docker, resulting in this warning:

```
WARNING: No output specified with docker-container driver. The build result will only remain in the build cache. To push the result image into the registry use --push or to load the image into docker, using --load
```

The  `docker push` in the Makefile won't succeed because of this when using the "docker-container" driver.

**What did you expect to happen:**

I would expect that a container image can be created and pushed regardless of which buildkit driver is used. 


**Anything else you would like to add:**

A simple fix is provided by https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/3062, which adds "--load" to every "docker buildx build" command. It should not make any difference when using the "docker" driver anyways (like on Linux), but it would help on other platforms that a subsequent push will succeed.
title: Add --load to "docker buildx build"

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]
Configmap documentation comments added as part of PR #3016. But the comments are automatically removed during the kustomize build. So the documentation comments no longer available to the users.

**Proposal**
We should follow the knative way of documenting configmap by introducing a field `_example` which contains a example configuration with documentation. As it is added as field kustomize wont remove the documentation comments. Here is an example configmap from knative.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-tracing
  namespace: knative-serving
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: knative-serving
    app.kubernetes.io/component: tracing
    app.kubernetes.io/version: devel
  annotations:
    knative.dev/example-checksum: "26614636"
data:
  _example: |
    ################################
    #                              #
    #    EXAMPLE CONFIGURATION     #
    #                              #
    ################################

    # This block is not actually functional configuration,
    # but serves to illustrate the available configuration
    # options and document them in a way that is accessible
    # to users that `kubectl edit` this config map.
    #
    # These sample configuration options may be copied out of
    # this example block and unindented to be in the data block
    # to actually change the configuration.
    #
    # This may be "zipkin" or "none" (default)
    backend: "none"

    # URL to zipkin collector where traces are sent.
    # This must be specified when backend is "zipkin"
    zipkin-endpoint: "http://zipkin.istio-system.svc.cluster.local:9411/api/v2/spans"

    # Enable zipkin debug mode. This allows all spans to be sent to the server
    # bypassing sampling.
    debug: "false"

    # Percentage (0-1) of requests to trace
    sample-rate: "0.1"
```

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

Headers are not handled and returned properly in v1/v2 endpoints in the recent master branch:

1. Headers are not returned in **v1 endpoints**

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/f9e9a079712e202e11855419a03b2966320fe575/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v1_endpoints.py#L74-L80

if the response is a `dict`, then the headers will be completely discarded.

in v2 endpoints, the headers are handled properly:

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/97bada50b5b3abe32b0dc618560735017ec2a070/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v2_endpoints.py#L146-L147

2. `dataplane.encode` completely discarded the response headers from the model

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/97bada50b5b3abe32b0dc618560735017ec2a070/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/dataplane.py#L259-L260

So any custom headers returned back from the model will be completely lost for **both v1/v2 endpoints**.

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/97bada50b5b3abe32b0dc618560735017ec2a070/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v1_endpoints.py#L76-L85

**What did you expect to happen:**

Custom headers should be passed through and returned properly, so things won't break if users upgrade their Python SDK to 0.11.x

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
After upgrading our kserve deployment from **`v0.9.0`** to **`v0.10.1`**, I noticed a significant performance degradation in latencies, which affects only xgboost models served by `kserve-xgbserver` ClusterServingRuntime. No changes to the model, model configuration or ClusterSertvingRuntime configuration were applied during the upgrade, so the only difference is the version of `kserve/xgbserver` image, that is used for serving models:
* `kserve/xgbserver:v0.9.0` – is used in Kserve release 0.9.0
* `kserve/xgbserver:v0.10.1` – is used in Kserve release 0.10.1

In order to isolate the problem and eliminate other moving parts from the suspicion list, I run a simple standalone load test of the `kserve/xgbserver` itself with a sample XGB model. To do so, I ran `kserve/xgbserver` on my local Docker runtime as this:
```bash
docker run --rm -it \
    -p 8080:8080 \ 
    -v ~/xgboost/model/:/mnt/models \
   kserve/xgbserver:v0.9.0 --model_name=my_model --model_dir=/mnt/models --http_port=8080 --nthread=1
```

Then, I executed `vegeta` load test to compare serving performance between v0.9.0 and v0.10.1:
```bash
vegeta attack -duration=1m --targets=./target.txt | tee results.bin | vegeta report
```

`target.txt` Content:
```
POST http://localhost:8080/v1/models/my_model:predict
@./request.json
```

The comparison of test results between 0.9.0 and 0.10.1:
* _**`kserve/xgbserver:v0.9.0:`**_
```
Requests      [total, rate, throughput]         3000, 50.02, 50.00
Duration      [total, attack, wait]             59.995s, 59.979s, 15.412ms
Latencies     [min, mean, 50, 90, 95, 99, max]  14.628ms, 16.535ms, 15.82ms, 18.181ms, 18.966ms, 22.101ms, 87.353ms

Bytes Out     [total, mean]                     36078000, 12026.00
Success       [ratio]                           100.00%
Status Codes  [code:count]                      200:3000
Error Set:
```

* _**`kserve/xgbserver:v0.10.1:`**_

Bytes Out     [total, mean]                     36078000, 12026.00
Success       [ratio]                           100.00%
Status Codes  [code:count]                      200:3000
Error Set:
```

Such a gap in observed latencies between 0.9.0 and 0.10.1 is persistent and reproducible over multiple test runs, different warm-up and test durations.

**What did you expect to happen:**
It doesn't seem like version of `xgboost` library has changed between Kserve release 0.9.0 and 0.10.1, so no performance degradation of the `xgbserver` is expected.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]

When running the `kserve.ModelServer` with more than one worker process, the resulting `/metrics` endpoint(s) only show the metrics contributed from its respective uvicorn worker process, rather than the cumulative metrics from **all** the uvicorn worker processes. The parent process load balancing makes this random, so the implication here is that any prometheus operator (on K8s or local/docker etc) would only ever see a fraction of the modelserver's emitted metrics - those of whichever uvicorn process it manages to reach at any given ping.

**What did you expect to happen:**

A cumulative metrics capture in the `metrics` endpoint of any and all uvicorn process fastapi applications, showing metrics from all active worker processes.

[To help us debug please run `kubectl get isvc $name -n $namespace -oyaml` and paste the output]

N/A

**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]

This was tested on local, so purely a python library issue (which has implications on metrics at cluster level regardless of deployment flavour and version)

Is this expected behaviour?[ `prometheus-client` lib offers multiprocessing support](https://github.com/prometheus/client_python#multiprocess-mode-eg-gunicorn) which I'm assuming addresses the above, but I havent had the time to read into it in detail.

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
In previous Kserve/Kubeflow versions, isvc had both internal and external url by default (external based on config-domain configmap from KNative serving namespace) and the VirtualService created for the isvc had 2 gateways configured by default - `knative-serving/knative-local-gateway` and `kubeflow/kubeflow-gateway`.

In Kubeflow 1.7, if you create an isvc, the virtualservice only has `knative-local-gateway` configured and hence isvc gets only internal URL. To get external URL and configure it with `kubeflow-gateway`, I had to explicitly update the config-domain configmap by running `kubectl patch cm config-domain --patch '{"data":{"example.com":""}}' -n knative-serving`.

I checked the inference-service configmap to make sure `kubeflow/kubeflow-gateway` is configured as ingressGateway.

**What did you expect to happen:**
Both cluster internal and external URLs to be available by default

**Steps to reproduce**
Install Kubeflow 1.7 and run through https://kserve.github.io/website/0.8/get_started/first_isvc/#run-your-first-inferenceservice.

When you get status https://kserve.github.io/website/0.8/get_started/first_isvc/#3-check-inferenceservice-status, you will see `sklearn-iris.kubeflow-user-example-com.svc.cluster.local` instead of `http://sklearn-iris.kubeflow-user-example-com.example.com`. Describe the VirtualService created for the isvc to confirm the above findings

**Anything else you would like to add:**

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Hi I have a kubeflow server running on EKS on AWS. I am trying to replicate the Iris example for Kserve. I have done this tutorial step by step: https://awslabs.github.io/kubeflow-manifests/docs/component-guides/kserve/tutorial/. I am using a cognito + rds + s3 setup.


This is my model training code:

```
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn import datasets, linear_model
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import joblib
#import sklearn.externals.joblib as joblib

# load the iris dataset
iris = datasets.load_iris()
X = iris.data
y = iris.target

# split the data into training and test sets
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)

# fit a linear regression model
reg = linear_model.LogisticRegression()
reg.fit(X_train, y_train)

# save the model to a file
joblib.dump(reg, 'model.joblib')
```
Now I have uploaded this model to an S3 bucket: s3://kubeflow-artelus/iris. 

This is my s3_secret.yaml file where I am creating the secret and the service account:

```

apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Create a simple kserve model:
```
import kserve
from typing import Dict
import argparse
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class CustomModel(kserve.Model):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.name = name
        self.load()

    def load(self):
        self.ready = True

    def predict(self,request: Dict, headers: Dict ) -> Dict:
        logger.info(request)
        return request


DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME = "custom-model"

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(parents=[kserve.model_server.parser])
parser.add_argument('--model_name', default=DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME,
                    help='The name that the model is served under.')

args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = CustomModel(name=args.model_name)
    kserve.ModelServer().start([model])
```
And when you run the server:
```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
sys:1: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AioServer.shutdown' was never awaited
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**
What worked for me is adding this line before initializing the model:
```
multiprocessing.set_start_method('fork')
```

The above issue only happens on mac, and does not seem to happen with linux containers, this is probably something to do with how to OS defaults to creating new processes.

Hence the parameters sent in the request do not exist anymore in the server side. 

Will write a dummy client and server code to further understand the problem

`client.py`

/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Hi! We've upgraded our kserve cluster from 0.9 to 0.10 and updated python kserve lib from 0.9 to 0.10. After that our custom model image couldn't start because of the below error:
`RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess. To use CUDA with multiprocessing, you must use the ‘spawn’ start method`
After explicitly setting 'spawn' method, image starts, but throws following error on every request to `/v1/models/custom-model:predict`:
`AttributeError: Can’t pickle local object ‘request_response.<locals>.app`

**What did you expect to happen:**
We've expected that our model continue to work on kserve v0.10 the same way as it worked on v0.9

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
```
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: avatar
  annotations:
....
  labels:
   ...
spec:
  predictor:
    containerConcurrency: 1
    timeout: 3600 # 60 min
    minReplicas: 0

    volumes:
    - name: avatar-bucket-key
      secret:
        secretName: avatar-bucket-key

        image: ***
        volumeMounts:

          mountPath: /var/secrets/google
        env:
...

          - containerPort: 8080
            protocol: TCP

          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            cpu: 10
            memory: 32Gi
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            cpu: 2
            memory: 16Gi
```

**Anything else you would like to add:**
I did a little bit of investigation, so I think below findings might help:
1. Accordingly to release notes of kserve v0.10, python lib start leveraging multiprocessing
2. pytorch: Multiprocessing in CUDA runtime doesn't work with 'fork' method -https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/multiprocessing.html#cuda-in-multiprocessing 
3. After changing multiprocessing start method to 'spawn' our custom model images was able to start, but could not handle the requests because of the error: `AttributeError: Can’t pickle local object ‘request_response.<locals>.app`
4. [As I see from source code](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/v0.10.0/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/server.py#L135), kserve uses uvicorn and it looks like uvicorn require different style of server initialisation when used together with multiprocessing in 'spawn' mode - https://www.uvicorn.org/deployment/#running-programmatically

body:
The version of the `kserve` package that is currently on PyPI (version `0.10`) violates the GPL license because it depends on [`table-logger`](https://github.com/AleksTk/table-logger), distributed under GPLv2 (you'll see that the library is now MIT, the author updated the license just a few days ago, but hasn't released a new version with the new license yet). No GPLv2 packages should be imported given that `kserve` has an Apache 2 license.


This was recently fixed by this PR https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/2673, which accidentally resolved the issue by replacing `table-logger` with `tabulate` (MIT License)

cc @yuzisun @cliveseldon @jinchihe @ellistarn 

Is it possible to quickly release a patch release `0.10.1` to include the above patch and make sure `kserve` is compliant with the Apache license? As it stands, any distribution and vendor using `kserve` is liable for a license violation.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

If you follow the [instructions](https://kserve.github.io/website/0.9/modelserving/v1beta1/custom/custom_model/#build-the-custom-image-with-buildpacks) provided on the documentation of Kserve, which requires you clone kserve repository as instructed here:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6526276/212365660-e7a0921f-d5b9-4cfe-877b-e48de9fdeea8.png)

It is never mentioned that you should go to a specific branch. What happens is that if you do as instructed and run

```bash
pack build --builder=heroku/buildpacks:20 ${DOCKER_USER}/custom-model:v1
```

Then you will actually be building a custom model that requires the latest release candidate, since it tries to use a function not found on the latest stable version of kserve. This funcion is `generate_uuid`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6526276/212366447-b7432d6d-65a9-4aae-94be-9fe0bb754fe9.png)

So we should either pin the versions found on `master` branch to the release candidates, or mention to use a specific branch that works. I'm happy to make a Pull Request to add this to the `requirements.txt` or simply add a note to the documentation.

¿

**What did you expect to happen:**

I'm expecting for master branch to contain a `custom-model` example that is able to get installed with the `python/custom_model/requirements.txt` which are simply unpinned `kserve` and `fastapi`. 

```bash
**kserve==v0.10.0-rc1
torchvision
fastapi==0.85.0**
```
work well. However, they only work with the `docs/samples/v1beta1/custom/custom_model/input.json` from master branch. 

Finally, `release-0.10`seems to work correctly. 

**What's the InferenceService yaml:**



**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]


**Environment:**

Istio Version: 1.15.3
Knative Version: 1.22
KServe Version: 0.8
Kubeflow version: 1.6
Cloud Environment: AWS EKS
Kubernetes version: 1.23
OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Amazon Linux 2 AMI

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
[A clear and concise description of what the bug is.]
Upgrading Python `kserve` library to [version 0.9.0](https://pypi.org/project/kserve/0.9.0/) caused a dependency conflict in our code base, due to `kserve` 0.9.0 [pins](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/2201) `protobuf` to 3.19.0 , and other parts in our code base require `protobuf` 0.20.0 or later.

**What did you expect to happen:**
We'd be able to use protobuf `0.20.0` or later.

We'd like to request `kserve` upgrading `protobuf` or relaxing the version requirement on this dependency, so that dependency conflict with other packages can be removed. Thanks!
title: kserve 0.9.0 requiring protobuf~=3.19.0 causing dependency conflict

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Running the sample notebook at https://github.com/kserve/kserve/tree/master/docs/samples/outlier-detection/alibi-detect/cifar10, could not get expected results.

The reason may be: Kubeflow 1.6 installs knative eventing 1.2.4, but this sample is based on knative eventing (0.18~0.22). After knative eventing 1.2, we do not have the `broker-ingress` service and the main concepts have greatly changed, this sample should be updated to adapt Kubeflow + knative eventing 1.2.

**Environment:**

- Istio Version: 1.14
- Knative Version: 1.2.4
- KServe Version: 0.8
- Kubeflow version: 1.6
- Cloud Environment: k8s_istio
- Minikube/Kind version: None
- Kubernetes version: (use `kubectl version`): 1.23
- OS (e.g. from `/etc/os-release`): CentOS 7
title: The outlier detection sample notebook is not compatible with latest kubeflow deployment

title: kserve-controller-manager crashing

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**

This details behavior I saw from testing https://github.com/kserve/kserve/pull/2589 where we add labels to metrics from kserve-container in queue-proxy before exporting the metrics on the prometheus port. The reason we need metric labels added at the queue-proxy level is because if someone is using these metrics to create a dashboard, the labels added in this PR will allow the user to create a dashboard using labels that match queue-proxy/serverlesss mode. If kserve is not using serverless mode, we do not need to add them. 

What this means: we scrape metrics from kserve-container and aggregate them with the queue-proxy metrics and then spit them out on the pod's defined prometheus port. 

The problem: there is some weirdness when converting the scraped metrics into golang object and then writing them back out. 

1. Built a new queue-proxy image, pushed it to local artifactory, and 
` make docker-build-qpext`
`docker push qpext:$TAG`
 
use qpext-patch.yaml 
```
data:
  queueSidecarImage: qpext:$TAG
```

to replace current qpext image with new, test image
`kubectl patch configmaps -n knative-serving config-deployment --patch-file qpext-patch.yaml`

2. I created a custom predictor that produces a simple output for testing
 
```
import kserve
import time
from random import randint
from typing import Dict


class CustomServerTestModel(kserve.Model):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.name = name
        self.load()
        self.ready = True

    def load(self):
        pass

    def predict(self, request: Dict, headers: Dict[str, str] = None) -> Dict:
        time.sleep(randint(1, 3))
        return {"prediction": [randint(1, 9)]}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = CustomServerTestModel("custom-server-test")
    kserve.ModelServer().start([model])
```

built image 
& made a service yaml 

```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: custom-test
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - name: kserve-container
        image: cusom-test:latest
```

3. This worked fine when I didn't add labeling logic in qpext. The metrics were in grafana/being scraped by prometheus. Next, I added labeling logic and completed step # 1 again. Now, no metrics populated in grafana. 

4. debug: ran local prometheus instance and found errors

created prometheus.yml
```
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: "test"
    scheme: http
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9088']
```

& ran ./prometheus --log.level=debug 

output: 
```
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:36.875Z caller=scrape.go:1335 level=debug component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=test target=http://localhost:9088/metrics msg="Append failed" err="invalid metric type \"untyped\""
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:36.977Z caller=compact.go:510 level=info component=tsdb msg="write block resulted in empty block" mint=1663617600000 maxt=1663624800000 duration=101.4859ms
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:36.978Z caller=head.go:844 level=info component=tsdb msg="Head GC completed" duration=1.088618ms
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:36.978Z caller=checkpoint.go:100 level=info component=tsdb msg="Creating checkpoint" from_segment=36 to_segment=37 mint=1663624800000
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:37.037Z caller=head.go:1013 level=info component=tsdb msg="WAL checkpoint complete" first=36 last=37 duration=58.584004ms
ts=2022-12-15T20:59:51.700Z caller=scrape.go:1335 level=debug component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=test target=http://localhost:9088/metrics msg="Append failed" err="invalid metric type \"untyped\""
```

some metrics are not converting correctly. 

5. Figuring out issue # 1 (header/format)

add testing logic in qpext, "if metric is UNTYPED, skip processing it"

ran prometheus locally again

output: 
```
caller=scrape.go:1335 level=debug component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=test target=http://localhost:9088/metrics msg="Append failed" err="data does not end with # EOF"
```

this is a new error - after some digging I found this is how open metrics format expects the file to end. 

Debugging steps:
* Next, I printed the format, which comes from the header and is set in the python SDK code. 
* The format is open metrics. 
* Next, I switched the method MetricFamilyToText -> MetricFamilyToOpenMetric. 
Still got error from prometheus scraper about #EOF. 
* After researching, seems like there is no clear way to fix this by forcing an #EOF after reading, so I decided to see if maybe the header was the issue. 
* Forced the header in the code to be text/plain and reverted to using MetricFamilyToText 

Result: no more #EOF issue. 
Summary: for some reason the format is being set as open metrics, but nowhere is it hardcoded. the python sdk code seems to gather what header should be set.  https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L72

6. Patching issue # 2 (untyped metrics) 

After fixing the #EOF issue, the untyped issue still persists.

I created a debug log that printed out each metric labeled untyped when it scrapes kserve-container and saw logs like 
```
"untyped":["python_gc_objects_collected_total","python_gc_objects_uncollectable_total","request_postprocess_seconds_created","request_predict_seconds_created"]


{"level":"error","ts":1671491136.8018808,"caller":"qpext/main.go:121","msg":"skipping this untyped metric family","metrics":[{"untyped":{"value":1.81}}],"mf":"name:\"process_cpu_seconds_total\" type:UNTYPED metric:<untyped:<value:1.81 > > ","stacktrace"...}
```

issue: for some reason some (not all) metrics with `_total` and `_created` are not converting correctly. The total is consistently a counter and created is a gauge. 

solution: created a helper method that attempts to convert a metric with total or created suffix into counter or gauge. 

7. rebuilt qpext with changes & now prometheus can scrape and I see the metrics populated in grafana. 

Note: I tested this with torschserve and triton and these errors did not occur - the grafana metrics always populated in grafana. debug logs showed that the header for these is set to text/plain natively. 

**What did you expect to happen:**

I expected the header from kserve-container to be text/plain, but if it was open metrics, for it to be converted correctly. 


things that confuse me: 
* the output of 9088/metrics looks normal, even when prometheus scraper complains (contains all metrics too..) - this is what originally took me so long to debug, because 9088 output always looked correct. 
* the metrics labeled as untyped have names suffixed with _total and _created, but it's not always the same set of metrics. 
* why does python sdk set the header as open metrics yet we get a format issue because the stream doesn't have #EOF at the end of the stream, which is required by open metrics format? (is this maybe the root cause of the issue?) 


**Anything else you would like to add:**

The current state of the qpext labelling is that its working, but I feel that I implemented a hack and would like to figure out the root issue. I suspect that python SDK https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L72 is exporting it in such a way that the golang code is having issues converting it into MetricFamily type. There is more support for reading/writing text than open metrics in the expfmt library. 

When I debug and print everything out, it doesn't make sense why it chooses these to label as untyped. I have looked through expfmt code as well and can't yet find the reason. 

The triton and torchserve metrics working fine with the add labels code also threw me for a loop. The differences, as I can tell, are (1) header passed in to qpext for the scraped metrics is text/plain (2) there are fewer metrics in general for triton and torchserve.

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
Configure kserve 0.9 in RawDeployment mode. Run an InferenceService with `metadata: {annotations: null}`.

The mutating web hook fails admission because https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/8fdd82fe109967efe94b7a012f07f9d75ab2eb60/pkg/apis/serving/v1beta1/inference_service_defaults.go#L86 doesn't check for nil annotations map before trying to setup a new annotation.

**What did you expect to happen:**

Kserve to be able to deal with an InferenceService in RawDeployment mode without annotations.


**What's the InferenceService yaml:**
From 
```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  generateName: inference-service-v2-
  labels:
    inference-service-test.cambridgeconsultants.com: "true"
  annotations:
    hello: ok
spec:
  predictor:
    triton:
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/torchscript"
      runtimeVersion: 20.10-py3
      env:
      - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS
        value: "1"
```

The workaround is to simply add a dummy annotation. Unfortunately `annotations: {}` didn't work. 🤷

**Environment:**

- KServe Version: 0.9
- Cloud Environment: EKS
- Kubernetes version: (use `kubectl version`): v1.21.14
- OS (e.g. from `/etc/os-release`): MacOs
title: Cannot run InferenceService in RawDeployment mode without specifying some annotations

body:
/kind bug

What steps did you take and what happened:
`InferenceService` Deployments fail to autoscale beyond 1 replica if other non-kserve controllers inject labels/annotations in deployment after it is deployed.

When deploying an `InferenceService` in `RawDeployment` mode:
1. KServe controller-manager creates the set of resources for the KServe application (Deployment, Service, HPA)
2. After the Deployment is created, another non-kserve controller adds its labels and annotations.
3. This annotation/label injection triggers Deployment Reconciliation.
4. The reconciled change is immediately overwritten by the non-kserve controller which re-adds its labels/annotations.
5. Step 3 occurs, preventing deployments from scaling beyond 1 replica.

What did you expect to happen:
1. KServe to ignore non-KServe labels and annotations during the Deployment Reconciliation process.
2. The ability to configure which parts of the `DeploymentSpec` are ignored for the purposes of Reconciliation e.g.`“Template.Spec.ServiceAccountName”`

We have an in-house patch which solves this issue by addressing the points above, which involves only considering KServe annotations and labels during reconciliation and adding more fields to the ignored fields during comparison.

Environment:
- Istio Version: 1.14.1
- KFServing Version: 0.9.0
- Kubernetes version: (use `kubectl version`): `Server Version: version.Info{Major:“1", Minor:“21+“, GitVersion:“v1.21.14-eks-fb459a0”, GitCommit:“b07006b2e59857b13fe5057a956e86225f0e82b7", GitTreeState:“clean”, BuildDate:“2022-10-24T20:32:54Z”, GoVersion:“go1.16.15”, Compiler:“gc”, Platform:“linux/amd64”}`
title: InferenceService Deployments cannot scale beyond 1 replica due to Reconciliation
